tours.execution_observability__description: Understand execution outputs, monitor agent health, and optimize with the Lab.
tours.execution_observability__execution_activ: The Activity tab tracks every agent execution with status, duration, cost, and detailed logs. Toggle to Metrics view to see trends, cost anomalies, and success rates over time.
Each row shows an agent run with status (green = success, red = failed), duration, and cost.
Browse your execution history and check the metrics toggle.
Toggle to metrics view to see cost trends, success rates, and anomaly detection.
tours.execution_observability__health_monitori: Monitor your agent fleet's health with real-time scoring. Each agent gets a heartbeat score (0-100) with grades: Healthy (80+), Degraded (50-79), Critical (<50).
One row per agent with a thin heartbeat bar; healthy agents are hidden by default so issues stay in focus — toggle Show all to reveal them.
Click a row for the success / healing / stability / budget breakdown, cost projection, and failure predictions.
Scan the Vitals Ledger table and expand a row for details.
tours.execution_observability__lab_arena__act_: Power makes a row the live config, the diff icon compares its prompt with the active version, and the sparkles icon hands it to Athena with an improvement brief (Breed and Evolve live there now). The Economics panel below ranks pairs by cost-per-success.
tours.execution_observability__lab_arena__base: The target icon pins a row as the regression baseline. The Δ column then shows every pair's gain or drop against it — a warning icon flags a drop big enough to be a real regression.
Pin a baseline, watch the delta
tours.execution_observability__lab_arena__desc: The Lab is a single table of every prompt version × model pair your agent has been measured on. The live config is marked Active, each row carries a rating plus a delta against your pinned baseline so regressions surface before you ship them, and row actions do the rest — measure in Arena, activate, diff, pin a baseline, or hand the version to Athena to improve.
tours.execution_observability__lab_arena__hint: Select an agent, open the Lab tab, and explore the versions table.
tours.execution_observability__lab_arena__meas: The flask icon on a row opens Arena scoped to that version — it sweeps the agent's use-cases on that model and fills in the Rating and Cost columns.
tours.execution_observability__lab_arena__open: Click the flask icon in the editor tab bar. Lab is Team-tier and up.
tours.execution_observability__lab_arena__sele: Lab works on agents that already have a promoted build — click one in the list to open its editor.
tours.execution_observability__lab_arena__vers: One row per prompt version × model pair. Every promote adds a version; Status shows which pair is Active (your live config), and a star in the Version cell marks the pinned baseline.
tours.execution_observability__messages_tab__d: After each execution, agents produce messages visible here. View them as a flat list or threaded conversations. Filter by priority and read status.
tours.execution_observability__messages_tab__h: Switch between flat and threaded views to see agent outputs.
tours.execution_observability__messages_tab__m: Messages show persona, priority (red = high), delivery status, and read state.
tours.execution_observability__messages_tab__t: Switch to threaded view to see conversation chains between agents.
tours.execution_observability__overview_dashbo: The Overview dashboard gives you a bird's-eye view of all agent activity. See success rates, active agents, pending reviews, and recent executions at a glance.
Explore the dashboard cards and metrics.
The activity feed shows your latest executions with status colors.
See success rate, active agents, and pending reviews at the top.
tours.getting_started__appearance_setup__descr: Before we begin, let's set up the app to feel right for you. Pick a theme, adjust text size, and set brightness to match your display. Changes take effect instantly.
tours.getting_started__appearance_setup__hint: Change at least one setting below to continue.
tours.getting_started__appearance_setup__narra: Welcome to Personas — I'm Athena, and I'll walk you through it. Let's start by making the app yours: pick a theme, nudge the text size, and set the brightness until it feels right. Change any one setting and we'll move on.
tours.getting_started__credentials_intro__brow: Click different categories in the catalog.
tours.getting_started__credentials_intro__conn: Notice the different auth methods: API Keys, OAuth, MCP, Desktop Bridge.
tours.getting_started__credentials_intro__desc: Personas connects to 200+ services out of the box — databases, messaging platforms, dev tools, AI providers, and more.
tours.getting_started__credentials_intro__hint: Browse the categories and click a connector to see its details.
tours.getting_started__credentials_intro__narr: This is your integration hub. Personas talks to over two hundred services right out of the box — databases, messaging, dev tools, and AI providers. Browse a category, then open any connector to see how it authenticates.
tours.getting_started__credentials_intro__view: Click any connector card to see its auth fields.
tours.getting_started__description: Set up appearance, explore connectors, and build your first AI agent.
tours.getting_started__first_execution__descri: Your agent is live. Open its Use Cases tab in the Agents module and run it once by hand — that's how you trigger any agent on demand, separate from its schedules and events.
tours.getting_started__first_execution__hint: Open the agent's Use Cases tab and run a use case.
tours.getting_started__first_execution__narrat: Last step — your agent is live, so let's run it once by hand. I've opened its Use Cases tab in the Agents module. Pick a use case and hit Run Now. This is how you trigger any agent on demand, separate from its schedules and events. When the run finishes, you've completed the tour.
tours.getting_started__first_execution__open_u: Your new agent's editor is open on the Use Cases tab — it lists every capability the agent can run.
tours.getting_started__first_execution__run_no: Pick a use case and click "Run Now" to execute it manually. The run streams its result inline.
tours.getting_started__persona_creation__answe: Launch the build and answer the clarifying questions as they come. When the draft is ready it runs a smoke test and goes live — then we'll run it together.
tours.getting_started__persona_creation__descr: Type what you want the agent to do — one line is enough. The build reads your intent and resolves the connectors, triggers, and capabilities for you.

Describe what you want in one line and the build resolves the whole spec — asking a few clarifying questions as it goes. Under the intent, the persona-core badge sets the agent's temperament: a mentality archetype plus Risk, Speed, Model, and Memory. Then it runs a smoke test and promotes.
tours.getting_started__persona_creation__hint: Describe your agent, then set its persona core.
tours.getting_started__persona_creation__narra: Now for the fun part — building your first agent. Just say what you want it to do, in one line. Under the box, the persona-core badge sets its temperament — pick a mentality archetype, then tune Risk, Speed, Model, and Memory. Hit build and it asks a few clarifying questions, fills in the whole spec, runs a smoke test, and goes live.
tours.getting_started__persona_creation__set_c: The badge under the intent is the agent's temperament. Pick a mentality archetype — Guardian is cautious and verification-first, Scout is fast and signal-hungry — then tune Risk, Speed, Model, and Memory. Optional, but it shapes how the agent thinks.
tours.getting_started_simple__appearance_setup: Choose a color theme and text size that feels comfortable. Changes apply instantly — try a few!
Change any setting below to continue.
Hi, I'm Athena — let's get you set up. First, pick a look you like: choose a color theme and a comfortable text size. Change anything and we'll keep going.
tours.getting_started_simple__credentials_intr: Your agents need access to external services to be useful. Add a connection — like a Slack workspace, email account, or API key.
Click "Add new" and follow the steps.
Your agents need access to the services you use to be helpful. Let's connect one — maybe a Slack workspace, an email account, or an API key. Pick a service and follow the steps.
Click any service to see how to connect it.
tours.getting_started_simple__description: Pick your look, connect a service, and create your first agent.
tours.getting_started_simple__persona_creation: Describe what you want your agent to do in plain language. The system will draft it for you, run a quick test, and let you promote it live.
Type a simple description like "Summarize my daily emails" or "Monitor Slack for urgent messages".

Time to create your first agent. Just describe what you'd like it to do in plain language — something like "summarize my daily emails." I'll draft it, run a quick test, and you can promote it live when it looks good.
When the smoke test finishes, click it to see what passed.
When the test report looks good, hit promote. Your agent is live.
Skim the matrix — each cell is a behavior the agent will follow.
tours.obsidian_brain__description: Install and connect Obsidian, walk every Brain tab — Sync, Browse, Graph, Cloud, Revitalize — and see where vault memory plugs into the rest of the app.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_browse_tab__dee: Launches the Obsidian app at the selected note via an obsidian:// link.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_browse_tab__des: A read-only explorer for the vault, inside the app. The folder tree shows note counts, the preview renders markdown with frontmatter lifted into a Properties row, and Open in Obsidian deep-links straight to the note.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_browse_tab__hin: Open a few notes; try the filter box and Open in Obsidian.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_browse_tab__nar: Browse is your window into the vault without leaving Personas. Click through the tree, preview any note, and jump to the real thing in Obsidian with one button.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_browse_tab__pre: Markdown rendered with tables and code; YAML frontmatter becomes a Properties chip row; word count in the header.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_browse_tab__tre: Collapsible folders with note counts. The filter box narrows the tree by file name.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_cloud_tab__desc: Optional off-site backup: push the vault's files to your own Google Drive under Personas/ObsidianSync/ — a free alternative to Obsidian Sync. Only changed files upload (content-hash diff), and the drive.file scope means Personas can only see files it created.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_cloud_tab__hint: Note the sign-in flow and the Push / Pull to Drive buttons.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_cloud_tab__narr: Cloud is belt and suspenders: back the whole vault up to your own Google Drive. It only sees files it created, and only uploads what changed.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_cloud_tab__push: Push uploads changed vault files; Pull downloads remote changes back into the local folder.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_cloud_tab__sepa: Drive backup treats the vault as an opaque file tree — it's separate from the app⇄vault memory sync.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_cloud_tab__sign: Sign in with Google, then Connect Google Drive — Personas requests the narrow drive.file scope only.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_cloud_tab__titl: Cloud — Back Up to Google Drive
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_graph_tab__capt: Append a section to today's daily note, or write a meeting note with attendees — straight into the vault.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_graph_tab__desc: The Graph tab is the vault's metrics-and-capture surface: aggregate stats (notes, links, orphans, Maps of Content), a relevance-ranked search, and quick capture into today's daily note or a structured meeting note. A file watcher keeps stats live while you edit in Obsidian.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_graph_tab__hint: Run a search, skim the orphan and MOC lists, try a journal capture.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_graph_tab__narr: Graph is where the vault becomes navigable: search it, find orphan notes that need linking, and capture thoughts straight into today's daily note. Agents get these same tools through the Obsidian Memory connector.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_graph_tab__sear: Relevance-ranked full-text search over the vault — the same tool agents call as vault_search.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_graph_tab__stat: Notes, links, orphans, MOCs, and daily-note counts — every result row opens the note in Obsidian.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_install__auto_c: Personas probes for the Obsidian desktop app the moment this step opens — when it's found, the step ticks itself off.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_install__descri: Obsidian Brain mirrors your agents' memory into an Obsidian vault — plain markdown notes you fully own, edit, and back up. This step checks whether the Obsidian desktop app is installed: if it is, the step completes by itself. If not, install it now — it's free.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_install__hint: If this step doesn't complete on its own, install Obsidian from obsidian.md, open it once to create a vault, then click "I've explored this".
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_install__instal: Download Obsidian free from obsidian.md (Windows / macOS / Linux), launch it once, and create or open any vault folder.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_install__narrat: Before anything else, let's make sure Obsidian itself is in place. I'm checking for it now — if you don't have it yet, grab it free from obsidian dot md, open it once to create a vault, and come right back.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_install__why_ob: Vendor-neutral memory: every agent memory becomes a readable markdown file in a folder you own — git it, Drive it, or read it in bed.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_memory_dimensio: Agents write memories → they land as notes → you edit, link, and prune them in Obsidian → the next Pull feeds your curated version back into the agent's reasoning.

The vault isn't a side feature — it plugs into the app's memory everywhere. Agents write memories you can curate in Obsidian; agents with the Obsidian Memory connector read the vault at runtime; opt-in mirrors copy Research Lab, execution knowledge, and Athena's brain into it; and the Director writes its coaching history there.
With the Director's long-term memory enabled, every verdict it writes lands in a Director/ folder — a durable, human-readable coaching log per agent.
Skim the dimensions below, then flip on any Knowledge mirror toggles you want.
Revitalize keeps all of the above lean — stale notes pruned, duplicates merged — so retrieval stays sharp as the vault grows.
Opt-in toggles (visible once a vault is connected): mirror Research Lab findings, per-persona execution knowledge, and Athena's brain into the vault as markdown.

Here's the payoff. Agent memories become notes you co-author — your edits flow back into how agents reason. Agents can search the vault live. Research, execution knowledge, and Athena's brain can mirror into it. And the Director keeps its coaching history there. One vault, every memory dimension of the app.
Attach the obsidian_memory connector to an agent and it can search the vault, walk wikilinks/backlinks, and append daily or meeting notes while it runs.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_revitalize_tab_: Start a pass and keep working — fuchsia dots on Plugins → Brain → Revitalize track it; re-opening the tab re-attaches.

Revitalize runs Claude over your vault in the background, the way sleep consolidates memory: prune stale notes, merge duplicates into canonical notes, refresh links and structure. A pass is bounded, narrates itself live, and ends with a summary — notes removed, merged, updated, and estimated tokens saved.
Prune stale notes, aggregate duplicates, refresh structure — plus optional free-form guidance.
Review the three goals, the live log area, and the Recent passes history.
Each pass ends with a stats card, and the Recent passes table keeps the last 20 runs — when, which vault, what was cleaned.

Memory needs sleep. Revitalize lets Claude tidy the vault in the background — pruning stale notes, merging duplicates, fixing links — while status dots track it in the sidebar. Every pass ends with a report of what got cleaned.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_sync_tab__descr: Sync is the two-way bridge. Push writes agent memories, profiles, and connectors into the vault as markdown; Pull reads your edits back into the app. When both sides changed the same note, a conflict card shows a line-level diff with Keep App / Keep Vault / Skip.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_sync_tab__hint: Look over the push selector, the pull button, and the sync log.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_sync_tab__narra: This is the bridge itself. Push sends memories into the vault as markdown. Pull brings your edits back — and that's the magic: edit a note in Obsidian, pull, and your agent now reasons with your curated version.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_sync_tab__pull_: Pull parses frontmatter back into the app. Conflicting edits show a blue/violet line diff above Keep App / Keep Vault / Skip.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_sync_tab__push_: Pick which personas to push with the chip selector — created / updated / skipped counts land in a result card.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_sync_tab__sync_: Every action is recorded — created, updated, conflict, skipped — with timestamps and the entity it touched.
tours.obsidian_brain__obsidian_vault_connect__: The Setup tab links a vault to Personas. Auto-detect scans the locations Obsidian itself knows about, Test verifies the folder is a real vault, and Save Configuration activates it. Already connected? This step completes by itself.
Scans Obsidian's own config for known vaults. You can also Browse to any folder manually.
Auto-detect (or browse to) your vault, press Test, then Save Configuration.

Now let's wire a vault in. Hit auto-detect — Personas reads the same registry Obsidian uses — then test the folder and save. Your vault list on the right remembers every vault you connect, so switching later is one click.
Choose what syncs — memories, persona profiles, connectors — and whether Auto-Sync fires on every memory write.
Persists the vault and adds it to the Saved Vaults list. This is what completes the step.
Verifies the folder has a .obsidian directory and counts its notes.
tours.orchestration_events__description: Chain agents together with events, triggers, and the visual event canvas.
tours.orchestration_events__event_chaining__ch: A→B chaining: A finishes → emits event → B's trigger matches → B executes. Chain B→C and you have a pipeline.
tours.orchestration_events__event_chaining__de: The chain trigger is the key to multi-agent workflows. Agent A completes → emits execution_completed → Agent B's event_listener fires → Agent B runs. Chain Studio's Compose tab lets you wire new chains: arm a source, pick a target persona.
tours.orchestration_events__event_chaining__ev: Sources column (left) lists every event type emitters can produce. The middle shows fan-out edges. Consumers (right) are agents subscribed to those events.
tours.orchestration_events__event_chaining__hi: In Chain Studio, sources are on the left, target personas on the right.
tours.orchestration_events__event_chaining__so: An event_listener with source_filter: "persona-a" only fires on events from persona-a. Without it, it fires on any agent emitting that event type.
tours.orchestration_events__events_intro__desc: Every action in Personas generates events — executions completing, webhooks arriving, schedules firing. The Overview > Events tab is the read-only log; the Events sidebar section is where you wire and inspect routing.
tours.orchestration_events__events_intro__even: Click any row to open the JSON payload viewer — that's exactly what listeners receive.
Each row shows an event with its type, source, target agent, and outcome status.
Try filtering: execution_completed, webhook_received, schedule_fired, manual_trigger, escalation, and the healing/incident events.
tours.orchestration_events__events_intro__hint: Browse the recent event log and try filtering by type.
tours.orchestration_events__live_stream__dead_: Events that exceeded retry caps land in dead-letter. The tab next to live-stream lists them — replay individually or in bulk after fixing the consumer.
tours.orchestration_events__live_stream__descr: The live-stream tab is the same event bus, but rendered in real-time. Use it to debug chains while they fire, watch a webhook propagate, or sanity-check rate-limits when something seems silently dropped.
tours.orchestration_events__live_stream__hint: Watch the stream tick. Trigger a manual execution to see the events arrive.
tours.orchestration_events__live_stream__strea: Filter by event type or persona to focus on a specific chain. Combine with the rate-limits tab when chains are dropping events.
Events appear top-to-bottom as they're published. Color codes match the Overview log — green success, red failure, amber warning.
tours.orchestration_events__trigger_types__des: Triggers define when an agent activates. PULL watches for changes (schedule, polling, file watcher, clipboard, app focus), PUSH receives signals (webhook, event_listener), COMPOSE combines them (chain, composite). Every agent has at least one — set when you build it on the Glyph.
tours.orchestration_events__trigger_types__hin: Look at how triggers are categorized, then see them wired on the Event Canvas.
tours.orchestration_events__trigger_types__see: The Events → Builder canvas (next step) shows every agent's triggers as a live routing graph — the clearest place to see what listens to what.
tours.orchestration_events__trigger_types__set: An agent's trigger is chosen during the build — the "When" row / Trigger sigil. Pick a schedule, a webhook, or an event to listen for; it's baked into the agent at promote time.
tours.orchestration_events__trigger_types__tri: Schedule, polling, file watcher, clipboard and app focus = Pull. Webhook and event_listener = Push. Chain and composite = Compose. Each family answers "what wakes this agent up?".
tours.plugins_explorer__description: Walk through every plugin in the catalog — Companion, Twin, Dev Tools, and the supporting cast.
tours.plugins_explorer__plugin_companion__auto: Toggle autonomous to let Companion act on its own when it has high-confidence suggestions. Manual review stays default.
tours.plugins_explorer__plugin_companion__desc: Companion is an always-available chat panel that knows about your agents, executions, and recent activity. It can answer questions, draft persona descriptions, and propose actions you can run with one click.
tours.plugins_explorer__plugin_companion__hint: Open the Companion panel (footer icon) and ask it about your fleet.
tours.plugins_explorer__plugin_companion__open: The companion icon lives in the footer. Click to expand the chat surface.
tours.plugins_explorer__plugin_companion__proa: Companion sometimes surfaces "Did you know?" cards inline. Engage or dismiss.
tours.plugins_explorer__plugin_dev_tools__desc: Dev Tools is the workspace-management plugin. Track local projects, scan a repo for idea seeds, triage the backlog, dispatch task-runners, map where each project calls an LLM, and watch your Claude Code sessions in the Fleet sub-tab. Useful when an agent's job is to wrangle code.
tours.plugins_explorer__plugin_dev_tools__dev_: Wire each project to an LLM-observability tool (Langfuse, LangSmith, Helicone, or LightTrack) to see where it calls an LLM — use case, provider, model, tokens and cost.
Register a local repo so agents can chat with its files, scan for issues, or run scripts.
Adopt preset scan skills into a project, dispatch them against contexts, and watch coverage + run history in the Analytics tab. Findings land as backlog ideas.
Dispatch tasks to remote workers (or Claude Code sessions). Watch progress with live logs.
tours.plugins_explorer__plugin_dev_tools__hint: Open Dev Tools and skim its sub-tabs.
tours.plugins_explorer__plugin_others__descrip: Two more plugins round out the production catalog: Drive (file sync) and Obsidian Brain (note-vault indexing + graph). In dev builds you'll also find Artist (image/video generation) and Research Lab (literature → hypotheses → experiments). Fleet — multi-session Claude Code orchestration — lives as a sub-tab of Dev Tools, not a standalone plugin.
tours.plugins_explorer__plugin_others__dev_ext: Artist (Leonardo + Blender + media studio) and Research Lab (structured literature reviews + experiments) ship in dev builds only — handy to know they exist.
tours.plugins_explorer__plugin_others__drive_o: Drive syncs files; Obsidian Brain indexes your vault for knowledge retrieval and graph navigation.
tours.plugins_explorer__plugin_others__hint: Browse each plugin from the catalog and enable any that look useful.
tours.plugins_explorer__plugin_twin__descripti: Twin captures your communication style, knowledge, and voice so agents can speak as you. Train it on past emails, set tone profiles, and route channels (Slack, email) through your twin.
tours.plugins_explorer__plugin_twin__hint: Open Twin and look at the eight sub-tabs.
tours.plugins_explorer__plugin_twin__twin_chan: Connect Slack/email so messages drafted by an agent get reviewed-as-you before sending.
tours.plugins_explorer__plugin_twin__twin_prof: Each profile is a distinct identity — "work me", "weekend me". Agents can pick which one to channel.
tours.plugins_explorer__plugin_twin__twin_tone: The Tone tab teaches the system how you write. The Voice tab handles audio cloning (Team+).
tours.plugins_explorer__plugins_browse__descri: Plugins extend Personas with new surfaces — image generation, repository tooling, Obsidian sync, research workflows, voice cloning, observability, and an AI companion. This is the catalog: toggle a plugin on and it shows up in the Plugins sidebar.
tours.plugins_explorer__plugins_browse__hint: Toggle one plugin on, then off — watch the sidebar nav react.
tours.plugins_explorer__plugins_browse__scan_c: Each card shows what the plugin does in one line. Disabled cards are dimmed; enabled ones get a colored border.
tours.plugins_explorer__plugins_browse__tier_g: Some plugins require Team tier or higher; the catalog still shows them so you can see what's available. (Artist and Research Lab are dev-build-only and are hidden from the catalog in production.)
tours.plugins_explorer__plugins_browse__toggle: Flip the switch on any plugin to add it to your workspace. The sidebar updates immediately.
tours.schedules_mastery__description: Read the schedules dashboard, switch between timeline and calendar views, and attach a schedule to an agent.
tours.schedules_mastery__schedules_attach__add: Open a use case and add a schedule subscription — choose cron or a fixed interval and set the frequency.
tours.schedules_mastery__schedules_attach__des: Schedules attach per use-case. Open an agent, go to its Use Cases tab, pick a use case, and add a schedule subscription — a cron expression or a fixed interval. It shows up here on the Schedules dashboard on the next refresh.
tours.schedules_mastery__schedules_attach__hin: Open an agent's Use Cases tab and schedule one of its use cases.
tours.schedules_mastery__schedules_attach__ope: Pick any agent from the list to enter its editor.
Each capability can run on its own schedule. The Use Cases tab is where you wire that up.
tours.schedules_mastery__schedules_attach__tit: Attach a Schedule to an Agent
tours.schedules_mastery__schedules_attach__ver: Navigate back to Schedules. Your new schedule appears with its next fire time and a fresh "active" badge.
tours.schedules_mastery__schedules_page__activ: Active triggers have a blue badge with the count. Paused ones sit grouped with a pause icon — useful when debugging chains.
tours.schedules_mastery__schedules_page__descr: Schedules is the at-a-glance view of every cron- and interval-driven agent in your fleet. It shows what fires next, what's paused, and lets you flip the global scheduler engine on or off.
tours.schedules_mastery__schedules_page__engin: The green/red badge in the header is the global scheduler. Pause it during deploys; resume to bring everything back.
tours.schedules_mastery__schedules_page__filte: Click a persona name in the sidebar to filter schedules to just that agent. The blue indicator shows when a filter is active.
tours.schedules_mastery__schedules_page__hint: Browse the active and paused schedules.
tours.schedules_mastery__schedules_views__back: If the engine was paused and you want missed runs to execute now, the Backfill modal on any schedule replays the window.
tours.schedules_mastery__schedules_views__cale: Click the view-tabs to switch to month/week. Hover any event to see persona, trigger config, and next fire time.
tours.schedules_mastery__schedules_views__desc: Two views of the same data. Timeline groups by time window (now, today, this week, later) — great for "what's about to fire?". Calendar shows month/week grids — better for "how dense is Tuesday?".
tours.schedules_mastery__schedules_views__hint: Toggle between Timeline and Calendar views.
tours.schedules_mastery__schedules_views__time: Default view. Groups by relative time so the next-to-fire schedule is always at the top.
tours.teams_orchestration__description: Walk the whole pipeline: register a repo, map its codebase, define success with KPIs, assemble a team from a preset, and put it to work on a goal — then see the orchestration model underneath (event-chains, assignments, shared memory).
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_context__d: A context-map scan reads the repo and organizes it into business-domain groups and per-feature contexts — each with its files, entry points, keywords, and API/DB surface. This map is the shared understanding the KPI scan and every agent reason over; without it they're working blind. The scan runs in the background and streams progress.
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_context__g: Each context card shows its files, keywords, and coverage badges (goals + ideas it produced).
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_context__h: On the Context Map tab, run the scan — then look at the groups and contexts it produced.
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_context__n: Next, map the code. The scan turns your repo into business-domain groups and per-feature contexts — the shared map your KPIs and your agents both read from.
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_context__r: Re-scan (incremental) maps only changed files since last time; Plan update schedules a weekly automatic scan.
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_context__s: It maps the repo in the background and notifies on completion — large codebases can take a few minutes.
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_kpi__descr: KPIs are the outcome layer above goals — what "working" actually means for the project. Scan for KPIs and Claude reads the context map to propose measurable metrics across technical / quality / traffic / value, grounded in the repo. Accept or adjust them. A KPI going off-track is what derives a goal for the team, so this is where you set the targets that steer the work.
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_kpi__hint: In Teams › KPIs, run "Scan for KPIs" and review the proposals it files.
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_kpi__narra: Now define what success means. Scan for KPIs and Claude proposes measurable metrics from your codebase. These are the targets — an off-track KPI is what tells a team there's work to do.
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_kpi__revie: Each proposal shows its measurement procedure + rationale; accept (optionally adjusting the target/cadence) or reject.
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_kpi__scan_: Claude reads the context map + connectors and proposes measurable KPIs across four categories.
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_kpi__steer: When a KPI drifts off its target, the loop derives a goal for the team — outcomes drive the work, not activity.
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_orchestrat: With a team in place, open the Monitor (press M) → Channels → Conversations, pick the project, and just describe the work in the composer. It reads as work rather than chat, so instead of posting a remark it decomposes the goal into routed steps and drops a proposal card in the conversation — confirm it and the team runs. Shared team memory and the project's KPIs keep the team converging instead of repeating itself. You set direction; the team does the work.
Plain language — "add tests for the billing module and open a PR". The composer decomposes it instead of posting it.
Press M → Channels → Conversations. Describe a piece of work in the composer and confirm the proposal.

Finally, put the team to work. Open the Monitor, go to the team's conversation, and describe the job in your own words. It routes the steps to the right agents and asks you to confirm — then runs them in parallel, pausing only when it needs you.
The proposal card shows each step and the agent it routed to. Run it to start; Drop to discard.
It becomes a live band in the conversation — step progress, rework rounds, pause/resume. Goals → Missions is the full mission-control view.
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_project__d: The pipeline starts by making a local code repository a first-class object the app can reason about. In Dev Tools › Projects, create a project: pick the folder, then under Source control bind it to a team (or a GitHub PAT) and pick the repo. Leave "Create Codebase connector" on — it wires a Codebase — <project> connector to the repo so agents read the right code.
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_project__f: The project name auto-fills from the folder; the field stays editable.
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_project__h: Click "New project" and walk the three-stage stepper: Project → Source control → Standards.
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_project__n: Everything starts with a repo. Register your project here, point it at the folder, connect your source control, and it becomes something the whole fleet can read and reason about.
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_project__s: Bind a team or a GitHub PAT, then pick the repo — this also provisions the Codebase connector.
Pre-commit gates, PR base branch, and auto-merge — the policy the team's agents will respect at run time.
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_team__bind: Adopting for your repo pins every member to it, so the whole team works the same codebase.
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_team__blue: The connection graph is the hero — toggle members on/off; sequential vs feedback edges are distinguished.
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_team__desc: Rather than wiring a team by hand, adopt a pre-wired preset — a best-practice roster with its connection graph already drawn (e.g. the Web Development Team). The blueprint graph is the include/exclude surface: tap a node to keep or drop a member, then adopt the subset in one pass. Pin the team to your project so every member reads the right repo.
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_team__gall: Each preset is a pre-wired team of agents for a workflow (e.g. an SDLC web-dev team).
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_team__hint: Click "Preset Team" to open the preset studio, then adopt one (e.g. Web Development Team).
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_team__narr: You don't have to build a team from scratch. Adopt a preset — a best-practice roster already wired together — pick which members you want, and you've got a working team in one pass.
tours.teams_orchestration__pipeline_team__titl: 4 · Assemble a team from a preset
tours.teams_orchestration__team_assignments__d: The newer mode: instead of pre-wiring every step, describe a goal in plain language in the team's conversation (Monitor → Channels → Conversations). The system decomposes it into a checklist, matches each step to an agent (manual / embedding / LLM), and runs them in a parallel DAG — pausing for your review only on failure. Every running mission is in Goals → Missions.
tours.teams_orchestration__team_assignments__g: "Review these PRs and draft a changelog" — the decompose step turns it into ordered, editable steps.
tours.teams_orchestration__team_assignments__h: Open Goals → Missions and read a goal → checklist breakdown.
tours.teams_orchestration__team_assignments__m: Each step is matched to an agent: manual (you pin), embedding (local cosine), or llm_eval (a Sonnet call picks).
tours.teams_orchestration__team_assignments__n: Sometimes you don't want to wire every step. Give the team a goal in plain language, and it breaks the goal into a checklist, picks the right agent for each part, and runs them in parallel.
tours.teams_orchestration__team_assignments__p: Up to max_parallel_steps run at once; failure pauses only that assignment, with inline Edit / Reassign / Skip.
tours.teams_orchestration__team_canvas_intro__: Shared instructions, default model profile, and budget caps cascade from the team to every member at run time.

A team is a set of agents plus the wiring that decides who runs, when, and with what shared context. The Team Canvas is where you compose it — persona nodes, connection edges, and per-team defaults. Roster membership and the runtime 'home team' anchor are distinct: an agent is placed on a team's canvas, and separately anchored to a team for its shared instructions and memory.
A connection means one agent's output can hand off to the next — the basis of event-chains (next step).
Open a team and look at the canvas — nodes are agents, edges are handoffs.
A team is more than a folder of agents. It's the wiring — who runs, when, and what context they share. This canvas is where you compose that.
Each node is a persona; its role and model overrides live in the node config.
tours.teams_orchestration__team_chaining__cond: Chain conditions (Any / Success / Failure / JSONPath) let a handoff fire only when the upstream output matches.
tours.teams_orchestration__team_chaining__desc: The original orchestration mode, and how most teams run today. An agent finishes → emits an event → a subscribed agent runs. There is no central driver — work propagates through the event bus. This is reactive and cheap; the handoff graph you wired on the canvas is what actually fires.
tours.teams_orchestration__team_chaining__emit: A completed execution publishes an event (e.g. execution_completed) with its output.
tours.teams_orchestration__team_chaining__hint: Trace one chain: which agent kicks it off, and who listens for its completion?
tours.teams_orchestration__team_chaining__list: An agent with a matching event subscription fires next. Wiring this subscription is what makes the chain real — miss it and the chain silently no-ops.
tours.teams_orchestration__team_chaining__narr: Most teams run as event-chains. One agent finishes, emits an event, and the next agent — listening for it — wakes up. No central conductor, just a relay.
tours.teams_orchestration__team_memory_goals__: Teams accumulate shared memory — decisions and constraints that get injected into every member's context on its next run, so the team converges instead of repeating itself. Link a team to a goal to track progress, and let the Director score executions and the Attention queue surface only what needs you. This is the 'set the direction, stay high-level' loop.
Tie the team to a tracked goal so progress, due dates, and stalls are visible — instead of running untracked.
Open the team-memory panel; note how decisions persist across runs.
A compact digest of the team's top decisions is injected into each member's prompt — shared context without manual hand-offs.
Teams remember. Decisions land in shared memory and flow into every teammate's next run. Link the team to a goal, and you can stay high-level while it converges.
The Director scores runs and the Attention queue raises only what needs a human — so you set direction, not babysit.
tours.templates_recipes__description: Adopt pre-built agents from the template gallery and reuse multi-step recipes across your fleet.
tours.templates_recipes__recipes_tab__descript: Recipes are multi-step prompt sequences you can run against any agent: "give it a code review checklist", "escalate to manager", "summarize the last 20 executions". They live separately from templates because they're cross-cutting, not agent-shaped.
tours.templates_recipes__recipes_tab__hint: Switch to the Recipes tab and browse the catalog.
tours.templates_recipes__recipes_tab__recipe_a: Once tested, attach a recipe to an agent so it runs automatically as part of that agent's playbook.
tours.templates_recipes__recipes_tab__recipe_p: Run a recipe against a real agent in a sandboxed playground — output is captured but not persisted to the agent's history.
tours.templates_recipes__recipes_tab__recipes_: Each card shows the recipe steps and inputs. Click to inspect the full prompt chain before running.
tours.templates_recipes__templates_adopt__conn: The adoption form lists required connectors. Click "Add" on each missing one to open the Vault picker inline.
tours.templates_recipes__templates_adopt__desc: Pick a template card → the adoption flow opens. It walks you through three things: credentials (which Vault connectors to attach), parameters (slots the template asks the user to fill), and review (final matrix before promoting).
tours.templates_recipes__templates_adopt__fill: Template-specific slots (Slack channel, GitHub repo, etc.) live below credentials. They become part of the prompt.
tours.templates_recipes__templates_adopt__hint: Click any generated template to start its adoption flow.
tours.templates_recipes__templates_adopt__pick: Click the most relevant card. Filters at the top help narrow by capability.
tours.templates_recipes__templates_adopt__prom: Review the rendered matrix → Approve. The agent goes live just like a hand-built one.
tours.templates_recipes__templates_page__descr: Templates are pre-built agents you can adopt with one click — the catalog covers ~200 patterns (research, monitoring, code review, support, etc). Adoption opens a guided form that asks only for credentials and parameters that template needs.
tours.templates_recipes__templates_page__gener: AI-curated patterns sorted by popularity and capability match. Each card shows required connectors as chips so you know what to set up first.
tours.templates_recipes__templates_page__hint: Browse the generated templates and the n8n importer.
tours.templates_recipes__templates_page__n8n_t: Got a working n8n workflow? Paste the JSON or drop the file — the importer translates nodes into a Personas agent draft.
tours.templates_recipes__templates_page__recip: Recipes are reusable multi-step plays (not full agents). We'll dig in next.
